top_stories.title: OpenAI's claimed proof of Navier-Stokes Millennium Problem sparks plagiarism allegations
points: OpenAI's model produced a 100-page proof that Navier-Stokes equations (fluid dynamics equations describing how liquids and gases move) can 'blow up' (become infinite in finite time), addressing one of math's seven Millennium Prize Problems worth $1 million.
The proof was generated in 88 hours using 10,000 parallel AI agents and verified with Lean (a proof-checking software).

NYU mathematician Tristan Buckmaster says he had shared his unpublished, year-long research on the same problem with an OpenAI mathematician; OpenAI's Sébastien Bubeck then announced a matching proof days later, which OpenAI denies stealing.
Buckmaster alleges OpenAI won't disclose if his drafts were used in training data and pressured him to publish solo, warning that including his Anthropic-employed co-author could hurt his career.
The proof has not undergone external peer review, raising questions about legitimacy and attribution.

unique_angles.point: Framed the achievement as suggesting physical laws could theoretically break down under certain conditions, calling it a top achievement in AI problem-solving.
Detailed the specific plagiarism dispute: OpenAI allegedly pressured Buckmaster to publish without his Anthropic co-author, threatening his career.
Named Sébastien Bubeck as the OpenAI researcher who announced the matching proof shortly after Buckmaster's disclosure.

top_stories.title: Meta launches Muse, an autonomous personal AI agent
points: Muse can autonomously send emails, book travel, make purchases, and sell items on behalf of users via an app, WhatsApp, or (later) Meta's AI glasses.
It integrates with third-party platforms like Spotify, Ticketmaster, Shopify, Gmail, and OpenTable.
A free tier has usage limits; paid tiers cost $20/month or $100/month for expanded capacity.
Security architecture includes running tasks in a sandboxed environment isolated from core execution, with a separate 'Sentinel' agent requiring approval before major actions run.

unique_angles.point: Noted Meta is positioning Muse's security design as an improvement after the company's past trust and privacy controversies.

Explained privacy protections in detail: Muse uses Stripe Link to generate single-use card numbers hiding real payment details, and isolates each user's web activity in a virtual machine to protect privacy even from Meta itself.

top_stories.title: Anthropic researcher quits, warns of existential AI risk
points: Jacob Coxon, who spent 3 years on AI pre-training at both Anthropic and OpenAI, resigned citing ethics concerns.

He warns both labs are racing toward superintelligence (AI systems that can upgrade and improve themselves with minimal human oversight) that could eventually hack anything and reshape the world overnight.
Anthropic's alignment lead Evan Hubinger estimates greater than 10% odds of AI ending humanity within the next decade and admits no clear safety plan exists.

unique_angles.point: Coxon's warning specifically framed the risk as AI potentially killing millions or everyone within a decade.

items.title: Apple unveils foldable iPhone
points: Apple's foldable iPhone features a 7.8-inch interior display after a decade of secretive development.
Priced between $1,999 and $2,199.

items.title: Google DeepMind's AlphaGenome Atlas
points: Maps 9 billion DNA variants with precomputed, single-number impact scores to accelerate disease research and treatment development.
Requires no coding or independent model-running, democratizing access to complex predictive models for scientists.

items.title: CPU shortage forces new capacity-planning practices
points: General-purpose compute has become a capacity-planning requirement most software teams at scale have never had to forecast before.
Teams must commit to CPU resources months in advance rather than scaling dynamically, changing infrastructure planning norms.
The shortage is pushing cloud-first software organizations to adopt traditional capacity-planning practices previously uncommon in their workflows.

items.title: Uber scaled AI agent usage 9.4x without raising costs
points: Between February and August 2026, Uber's agent requests grew 9.4x and users grew 7x, yet AI spending stayed flat after April; one model's cost per session dropped 52% from its peak.
Uber separated spending drivers into user adoption, workload, and token pricing, then optimized agent efficiency, the one lever they controlled.

Key tactics: dynamic model routing (sending jobs to the cheapest model that works), delegating simple subtasks to cheaper subagents while reserving powerful models for complex plans, and caching context for 1 hour to match engineer workflows, cutting tokens per query by 50%.

items.title: U.S. accuses Chinese AI firms of copying American models
points: U.S. government accuses six Chinese AI firms, including DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, and Alibaba, of using distillation (training smaller, cheaper models by learning from a larger proprietary model's output) to copy variants of Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and SpaceX models.
Officials say the copying likely occurred with Chinese government awareness and warn it could strengthen China's military and cyberattack capabilities against the U.S. and allies.
Allegations surfaced just before Xi Jinping's planned late-September U.S. visit, adding diplomatic tension.

items.title: Google and Janelia map a complete fruit fly brain connectome
points: Google and Janelia Research Campus published a complete wiring map (connectome) of an adult fruit fly's brain.
The map charts 166,000 neurons and 125 million synapses using electron microscopy and AI reconstruction.
